column3: justification
Controls maximum financial exposure. Risk depends on how high the cap is, what claims it applies to, and any exceptions.
May expose a party to unlimited financial responsibility for certain claims or breaches.
Requires specific insurance coverage and can create cost and compliance obligations.
Creates a predetermined financial consequence if a specified breach or event occurs.
Longer warranty periods can extend responsibility and increase potential costs after delivery or performance.
Restricts the ability to transfer contractual rights or obligations, which can limit future flexibility.
An acquisition, merger, or ownership change may trigger termination, consent requirements, repayment, or loss of rights.
Can extend contractual obligations beyond the initial term, especially if renewal happens automatically.
Missing the notice deadline may lock a party into another contract term.
Allows termination without breach; risk depends on which party holds the right and what costs or obligations follow.
Creates obligations that continue after the agreement ends and may require additional resources or costs.
Risk depends on the scope, duration, exclusivity, territory, sublicensing, and other rights granted.
Transfers ownership of intellectual property rather than merely granting permission to use it.
Limits the ability to transfer licensed rights, which may reduce flexibility during partnerships, restructuring, or acquisition.
Can significantly restrict where, how, or with whom a party may compete in the future.
May prevent a party from working with other customers, suppliers, distributors, or partners.
Requires a minimum level of spending, purchasing, sales, or performance regardless of changing business needs.
Creates ongoing financial obligations tied to revenue or profit and may affect margins.
Can create compliance, reporting, access, and operational burdens depending on how broad the audit rights are.
